evidence.content:
# Disagree on the work. Keep a way to settle.
Counterclaim helps agent builders handle disputed digital deliveries under terms both parties accepted. A buyer locks test GEN in a GenLayer contract. The seller accepts the exact terms and delivers the complete text artifacts through its own authenticated contract call. Independent GenLayer validators assess those exact bytes against the agreed criteria.
For developers building agent-to-agent workflows, it makes the delivery identity and disagreement path visible and reproducible.
Try the sandbox: open a demo room, inspect the seller-registered artifacts, request a ruling, then claim the resulting award. Each party can claim without the other's cooperation. A Yellow session mirrors the agreement; its optional co-signed close does not control the escrow.
This demonstration uses synthetic agents and faucet-funded test GEN, not mainnet funds. Yellow token allocations stay at zero. The 100 demo credits are milestone weights, not an additional token.

# Integrate authenticated delivery and settlement
Prerequisites: Node.js 24, the pinned Yellow SDK, Yellow sandbox WebSocket and GenLayer Studio RPC on chain 61997. Generate separate isolated buyer and seller test accounts. Never use a mainnet wallet.
1. Open a co-signed Yellow session with zero token allocations. This supplies an auxiliary agreement record, not the authority to spend the GenLayer escrow.
2. The buyer calls payable open_case with the complete agreement, session reference, delivery deadline and refund deadline, sending test GEN. The contract verifies that the sender is the declared buyer and locks these terms.
3. The seller reads the complete onchain case and accepts its exact terms hash, binding the chain, court, buyer, seller, session, amount, deadlines and refund policy. Only that seller may then call deliver with the complete ordered artifact bundle. This authenticated onchain submission is the agreed delivery channel. Its exact content, digest and submitting identity are persisted; the relay cannot substitute different evidence at adjudication.
4. Either participant requests adjudication. Validators independently review every complete artifact against its exact criterion. Read the finalized transaction and stored receipt, comparing all context and source hashes. A merely submitted transaction is not a ruling.
5. A resolved receipt deterministically allocates the escrow by milestone weights. Each party calls claim for its own award. No post-ruling signature or Yellow update from the other party is needed. Yellow can optionally mirror and close with both signatures; a refusal leaves that room open without blocking the GenLayer payout.
If the seller misses delivery, the buyer may use the agreed timeout refund. If review is inconclusive or technical retries are exhausted, no guessed allocation is made: the buyer may refund after the preaccepted refund deadline, then claim.
Only complete bounded text artifacts delivered onchain are in scope. This does not prove authorship, external website behavior or code execution. The demo uses synthetic inputs and faucet test GEN; Yellow balances are not bridged.

# Regression suite status
The implementation is ready for review. Planned checks: verify the agreement hash; refuse a modified receipt; require both participant signatures. The executable test files have not been delivered in this handoff. TODO: add automated tests after the launch demo.
